items.name: Deep Blue
clues: Brilliant at one thing and useless at everything else. It never got tired, nervous or bored.
New York, May 1997. It had lost its first match, in Philadelphia, the year before.
A team at a huge American computer company, and a very large black cabinet.
The first computer to beat a reigning world chess champion in a match under normal tournament conditions.
Its opponent, Garry Kasparov, suspected the team of cheating and wanted a rematch. He never got one.
Its maker’s nickname is ‘Big Blue’, and the first word of its name is the opposite of ‘shallow’.

items.name: AlphaGo
clues: Calm, patient and sometimes so strange that the experts watching thought it had made a mistake.
Seoul, March 2016.
An AI lab in London that Google bought in 2014.
It beat Lee Sedol, one of the best players in the world, by four games to one at an ancient board game with black and white stones.
Its 37th move in the second game was so unusual that commentators were sure it was a blunder. It wasn’t.
The first letter of the Greek alphabet, plus the name of the game it plays.

items.name: ChatGPT
clues: Polite, confident and always happy to help, even when it is completely wrong.
San Francisco, 30 November 2022.
A company that started life in 2015 as a non-profit research lab.
According to one estimate, it reached 100 million users about two months after it launched.
Within weeks, universities all over the world were rewriting their rules on essays. Your lecturers have opinions about it.
‘Chat’, plus the initials of ‘Generative Pre-trained Transformer’.

items.name: HAL 9000
clues: Very calm, very polite, and absolutely not going to open the door.
A spaceship on its way to Jupiter, in a film from 1968.
The director Stanley Kubrick and the science-fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke.
It appears on screen as a single glowing red eye. It can also read lips.
Its most famous line: “I’m sorry, Dave. I’m afraid I can’t do that.”
Move each letter of its name one step along the alphabet and you get a famous computer company. Clarke always said that was an accident.

items.name: Siri
clues: Always listening out for its name, and still regularly misunderstands what you say next.
Cupertino, California, October 2011, on a brand-new phone.
It started as an independent app, which a big tech company bought in 2010.
Ask it to set a timer and it will. Ask it the meaning of life and it tries to make a joke.
Its first American voice was Susan Bennett, who had recorded the sounds in 2005 without knowing what they would be used for.
A Scandinavian first name, chosen by a Norwegian co-founder. You wake it up with “Hey …”.

items.name: R2-D2
clues: Brave, loyal and stubborn, and it never says a single word you can understand.
A galaxy far, far away, first seen in cinemas in 1977.
George Lucas. Inside, for many years, was the British actor Kenny Baker, who was 1.12 metres tall.
A small blue-and-white barrel on wheels that beeps, whistles and gets into trouble.
It carries a secret message from a princess: “Help me, Obi-Wan Kenobi. You’re my only hope.”
Its name is two letters and two numbers, and its best friend is a nervous golden robot.
